# Fair but hard: certified unique-solution puzzles generated by language models

This repository contains the code, data, results and manuscript for a study of a
**generate → encode → certify** loop for logic puzzles:

* language models write or encode puzzles (zebra puzzles in English, Sudoku, Killer Sudoku, Futoshiki);
* two independent model encodings of the same text are proved equivalent with z3 (dual encoding);
* a SAT solver (MiniSat via PySAT, cross-checked with OR-tools CP-SAT) proves the puzzle has exactly one solution;
* a ladder of five nested deduction engines (unit propagation → single-constraint GAC → failed-literal
  probing → two-level lookahead → search) grades every puzzle, alongside solver statistics and
  minimal-unsatisfiable-core explanations for every fact.

Experiments: E1 faithfulness of LLM encodings (298 zebra puzzles, 3 encoders), E2 validity of
LLM-written puzzles with and without the solver loop, E3 ladder vs solver metrics vs accuracy of
Haiku/Sonnet/Opus, E4 evolution of fair-but-hard puzzles against a solver, E5 genres invented by an LLM.

The manuscript is `paper/main.pdf`. The benchmark release is in `benchmark/` (see its `DATASHEET.md`).

## Layout

| folder | content |
|---|---|
| `src/` | pipeline: CSP/CNF core (`csp.py`), ladder and metrics (`grading.py`), DSL (`dsl.py`), families, generation, experiments `e1_*.py` … `e5_*.py`, analysis, figures, `make_numbers.py` |
| `tests/` | unit tests (`pytest`) |
| `configs/config.json` | seeds and every experiment parameter |
| `data/` | puzzle banks (`data/bank/*.jsonl`), every LLM task file and output (`data/llm_tasks/<stage>/`), evolution states |
| `results/` | analysis outputs (JSON/JSONL), call ledger (`ledger.jsonl`), cost summary, tool-call audit |
| `figures/` | publication figures (PDF + PNG) |
| `benchmark/` | released puzzles with certificates, levels, metrics, explanations |
| `paper/` | LaTeX source, `numbers.tex` (generated), `references.bib`, `main.pdf` |

## Reproduce

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
pytest -q                                   # 17 tests
python -m src.build_bank                    # certified banks (seeded; takes a while on 4 cores)
python -m src.bank_stats
```

Every LLM stage works the same way: a script writes one task file per call into
`data/llm_tasks/<stage>/`, the call writes `<call_id>.out.json`, and running the script again
collects the outputs and continues. With an API key, pending calls of a stage are run with

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...                # never commit keys
python -m src.llm api <stage>
```

Order of stages (each command is re-run after its calls are done):

```bash
python -m src.e1_faithfulness prepare_paraphrase   # then prepare_encoders, then analyze
python -m src.analysis_e1
python -m src.e2_validity prepare_gen     # then prepare_enc, prepare_repair1, summarize
python -m src.e3_difficulty select|prepare|score && python -m src.analysis_e3
python -m src.e4_evolution        # zebra run (repeat until done), then: python -m src.e4_evolution heldout
python -m src.e4_evolution e4s    # Sudoku run, then: python -m src.e4_evolution e4s heldout
python -m src.e5_genres prepare   # then run, prepare_solve, score_solve
python -m src.fig_example && python -m src.fig_e1 && python -m src.fig_e2 && python -m src.fig_e3 \
  && python -m src.fig_e4 && python -m src.fig_gallery
python -m src.export_benchmark
python -m src.cost && python -m src.make_numbers
cd paper && latexmk -pdf main.tex
```

All model outputs used in the paper are committed, so the analysis, figures, numbers and PDF can
be rebuilt without any model call. Every number in the paper comes from `paper/numbers.tex`,
written by `src/make_numbers.py` from `results/`.

## How the model calls were made, and what a full run costs

Every call goes through the Anthropic Messages API (`src/llm.py`: `claude-haiku-5-5`,
`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-5-5`, adaptive thinking, effort `high`, 128k output limit,
8 calls in parallel). Exact input/output tokens, stop reason and message id of every call are
logged in `results/ledger.jsonl` and summarised in `results/cost_summary.json`. One experiment can
be run end to end with

```bash
PYTHONUTF8=1 python -m src.rerun_api e1      # or e2, e3, e4b, e4s, e5
```

(`PYTHONUTF8=1` matters on Windows, where Python otherwise reads and writes files as cp1252.)

* Calls behind the reported results: 672, 8.4M tokens, about **$38** at list prices.
* All calls including discarded runs: 971, about **$63**. Two runs were discarded: solving with
  4-5 puzzles per call (Haiku hit the output limit and Sonnet guessed, so accuracy depended on the
  batch; now one puzzle per call, `configs/config.json`), and an E4 run whose answer collector did
  not accept single-puzzle replies without the JSON wrapper (fixed in `src/solve_stage.py`, with a
  test). Both are kept in `data/llm_tasks_archive/`, `data/archive_*` and `results/archive_*`.
* An earlier version of the study, made without an API key, ran the same task files through Claude
  Code subagents; its outputs are on the `main` branch and its ledger is
  `results/ledger_subagent.jsonl`. Only the abandoned E4 pilot (`data/e4`) still comes from it.

The study is deliberately small (298 / 100 / 116 puzzles in E1 / E2 / E3).
